name: Contre-Jour Rim Portrait
description: One hard gridded strobe hidden directly behind the model's head fires forward into camera, so a single source produces two opposite material responses: thin flesh transmits it — the ear helix and lobe glowing translucent coral-red — while brushed metal reflects it as one elongated streak. The backdrop sits unlit and four stops down.
lighting: Hidden contre-jour rim, single hard gridded source
subject: person
prompt: a person in a sheer white cotton-poplin shirt over an oatmeal ribbed tank, lit by one hard gridded strobe hidden directly behind the head firing forward into camera, the head physically eclipsing the source so no flare enters the frame, thin flesh transmitting the light so only the ear helix, ear lobe and nostril wings glow translucent coral-red while the rest of the face stays its own warm olive tone, backlit hair resolving into separate flyaway filaments with dark gaps between them and never a solid glowing outline, a white polystyrene bounce camera-left returning soft directional fill so the face reads two and a half stops under the rim, an unlit warm putty-grey seamless paper sweep sitting four and a half stops down so the rim separates hard against it, genuine skin texture with visible pore structure and natural asymmetry, matte skin with narrow satin only where facial oil sits, never plastic or waxy, no second person, no visible rig, the frame filled edge to edge with no border or letterbox
